subject: Private cluster: persistent throughput degradation — exec readiness & tuning ask
body:
From: Olivia Parker <olivia.parker@edgehaven.ai>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: infra@edgehaven.ai
Date: 2026-11-28T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Immediate: sustained throughput drop on private cluster

Hi Karthik —

We're seeing a sustained ~30% drop in inference throughput across our private VPC cluster starting ~06:00 PT this morning. P95 went from ~450ms to ~1.2s and a growing number of requests are getting 503s. This is happening for the quantized gpt-small model pinned in our account (model id: eh-gptq-v2).

We've collected service logs and a heap of profiler traces — attaching the bundle (svc_logs_1128.tar.gz). Impact: our customer-facing feature is throttling back and some customers are complaining about timeouts. We need urgent help identifying a short-term mitigation and a safe tuning path.

Key notes:
- Cluster is on-prem (r5-gpu nodes) with Dedicated Private control plane (VPC).
- No recent deploys from our side in the past 48h.
- We did see one maintenance window yesterday for a kernel security patch on the host nodes.

Can we get Redwood ops/engineers to triage? If this needs exec attention we can pull in our COO but would like Redwood to lead the technical mitigation.

Thanks —
Olivia
Olivia Parker
Head of Platform, EdgeHaven

-----
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Parker <olivia.parker@edgehaven.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-28T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Immediate: sustained throughput drop on private cluster

Hi Olivia — thanks for the data and the log bundle. We're on it. Initial ask: can you confirm whether your infra team enabled the recent host kernel update across the pool or only a subset? Also, please keep the run of requests that result in 503s if possible (we'll need the full request/response pairs).

Marissa is pulling an ops runbook and I'll loop in our runtime team for a quick kernel/quantization check. Short-term plan: 1) collect KV cache stats and GPU utilization snapshots, 2) attempt a temporary fallback to the last working model variant (eh-gptq-v1) routed only for the most latency-sensitive routes, 3) prepare a canary tuning patch that adjusts the continuous-batching window and decoder prefetch.

I'll assemble a short exec-ready brief if we need an SLA/credit conversation. Can we schedule a 30-minute async huddle later today?

-Karthik
SVP, Customer Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-29T08:30:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Immediate: sustained throughput drop on private cluster

Team —

I dug into the logs (svc_logs_1128.tar.gz). Summary:
- GPU saturation is NOT across the board; it's concentrated on two nodes in the hot shard.
- There are sharp increases in kernel reschedules and nvml GPU memcpy stalls around 06:05 PT.
- KV cache hit-rate dropped ~14%, likely due to a small change in request prefixes after an SDK patch on the customer side.

Hypothesis: the host kernel update changed scheduler timing and exposed a contended NVLink memcpy path for the quantized runtime. Combined with lower KV cache hit-rate, the runtime's continuous-batching latency tail worsened and batch sizing became unstable.

Short-term mitigation I recommend:
1) Pin the hot shard to the previous kernel (rollback on the two affected nodes) OR set the kernel parameter that reverts the aggressive preemption introduced by the patch.
2) Force a temporary model route to eh-gptq-v1 for 25% of traffic (latency-sensitive) while we validate runtime flags.
3) Apply a tuning patch (attached) that reduces batch aggregation window from 12ms -> 6ms and disables opportunistic NVLink prefetch on the quantized path.

I've attached a concise tuning runbook: tuning-runbook-edgehaven-v1.pdf — it includes exact CLI commands, risk matrix, and rollback steps. We should treat the node kernel rollback as the higher-risk action; the runtime flags are lower risk and should be our immediate canary.

[Attachment: tuning-runbook-edgehaven-v1.pdf]

- Marissa
Principal Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

-----
From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-29T14:20:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Immediate: sustained throughput drop on private cluster

Marissa — good triage. Two follow-ups from the runtime metrics:
- The decoder queue growth correlates with a backlog in upstream request buffering; reducing batch window will lower p95 but could raise per-token cost by ~6-8% during the canary.
- If EdgeHaven needs to avoid any change to model variants, we can do a routing fallback to a hosted equivalent (hosted-gptq-e2) for a small percentage of traffic; that prevents on-prem node pressure but requires data egress consent.

We should flag this as an exec-level SLA risk: if 503s persist beyond 24h, we will need to discuss a customer credit and a prioritized hotfix schedule. I'll prepare the numbers for the exec brief.

-Jonas
Head of Runtime Engineering

-----
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Parker <olivia.parker@edgehaven.ai>, Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@edgehaven.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-30T11:00:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Immediate: sustained throughput drop on private cluster

Olivia / Rajiv —

Thank you for the quick data. Based on our triage above, Redwood proposes the following staged mitigation plan (low-to-high risk):

1) Immediate canary (1-2 hours): apply the runtime tuning flags from tuning-runbook-edgehaven-v1.pdf to the hot shard only (reduce batch window; disable NVLink opportunistic prefetch). Risk: minimal, immediate p95 improvement expected.

2) If canary improves p95 but 503s persist on other nodes: temporarily route 20% of latency-sensitive traffic to hosted-gptq-e2 in us-west (requires explicit data egress sign-off). This reduces on-prem pressure while preserving user experience.

3) If canary fails: schedule node-level kernel rollback on the two affected hosts during a 60-minute maintenance window (high risk — requires EdgeHaven approval).

Operational asks for EdgeHaven:
- Approve the canary immediately so our engineers can patch the hot shard (I have Marissa as lead on that).
- If you want an exec-level sync, propose a 30-minute slot today 16:00 PT; I'll bring a short 1-slide summary and the SLA exposure numbers.

I've opened Jira EH-1023 and populated the runbook and logs: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/EH-1023.

If you approve the canary, I'll kick off the patch and send runbook steps and post-change metrics to this thread.

Best,
Karthik
SVP, Customer Engineering
Redwood Inference

We can do the 16:00 PT exec sync today — please send calendar invite. We'll have Rajiv and our lead infra engineer on the call.

Olivia
